newsitem.title: INDIA: India ITC officials denied bail.
newsitem.headline: India ITC officials denied bail.

text.p: An Indian court on Tuesday denied bail to four ITC Ltd officials and two former chairmen of the tobacco firm, and remanded them to judicial custody until November 26, court officials said.

Calcutta's chief metropolitan magistrate A.K. Dasgupta rejected the bail plea of former chairmen K.L. Chugh and J.N. Sapru, saying the charges were serious and the accused would remain in custody to prevent any tampering with evidence.
"The charges are serious and they struck at the root of country's economy," Dasgupta said. "There is every chance that the accused may tamper with the evidence once they are released on bail."
Chugh and Sapru were arrested on November 1 for alleged foreign exchange violations.
Lawyers for Chugh and Sapru said their clients needed to be released on bail to receive unspecified medical treatment. But the judge said they were receiving care in a government hospital.
Lawyers for the Enforcement Directorate argued that the two should not be given bail as the agency wanted to examine evidence gathered after they were remanded to judicial custody.
The lawyers said a number of people had been arrested and incriminating documents had been seized after the six accused were taken into custody.
